comment: love him. so smart. so fun. loved this class so much

Prof. Ashe is super smart and a great guy, but his class was extremely boring because all we did was sit in a circle and talk about one book. Grade was only based on participation and three papers. Definitely only take ENG299 if you're planning on being an English major, because otherwise the class is excruciating.
Awesome professor. He had so much knowledge and experience and really knew what he was talking about. He's one of those professors I would recommend anyone to take

I enjoyed taking this class with Dr.Ashe as an SSIR course, but please know that he does assign a decent amount of readings and videos to watch per class. Granted that the class does only meet once a week the work load does make sense. We had 2 papers throughout the year each about 10 pages long, which wasn't bad. No daily graded work. Participate!

Professor Ashe is a very nice guy, but he assigns so much reading. Within a two day span he will assign over 200 pages. Also participation is over 30% of your grade, so you better make sure you read. Only a couple papers all semester, but one of them is a 10 pager. Not the worst class you could be in, but definitely not the best either.

Such a smart guy. His classes are all discussion based which I love. Stay engaged, participate, and do the readings. Lots of reading assignments but such intriguing stuff and engaging classes its worth it. first 9 am class I don't feel like I'm falling asleep in
He's such a respected and smart person I've ever met before.

Dr. Ashe graded very tough on our mid terms and mid term participation check in, but was more lenient with final grades. The mid terms are a good wake up call, too. You also learn a lot about an interesting topic.

Everyone should take Dr. Ashe once. The man is a genius, and his topics are interesting. You only have 3 grades, a 5 page paper (15%), a 10 page paper (50%), and participation (35%). Tough grader and you must participate. The outside readings aren't actually too long which is nice. I think he's fascinating professor, but I'd only want him once.
He is very difficult in his grading and during lectures he expects certain answers, so it can hard to have "good" participation.

His class is made up mostly of discussions and it is a MUST to participate, as class participation makes up 30% of your grade. There are only 2 papers, with the final being another take-home paper. He can be slightly unclear sometimes but if you ask questions he will always be more than happy to clarify.
He is very smart but narrow-minded. He has a specific answer he wants to hear and won't like your answer if it is not his. He is a VERY tough grader.

Ashe is one of the smartest people I've ever met, but that can be a good and a bad thing. I felt like I learned a lot in his first year seminar, but he's very narrow-minded in his thinking. Basically, if you don't agree with him, you're wrong. The two papers were also pretty tough, but doable.

Classes revolving around his research interests (post-blackness, black style) function as an ego booster for him -- the whole class was based on his book. Met with him about a paper, got my topic approved, and still got a "Not Graded" because he claimed it didn't fit his narrow expectation. Also, just a harsh grader in general no matter the class.

Ashe is a heavy seminar-style professor. The questions he throws into discussion can be sort of long-winded, but overall he's a great critical thinker & expands conversations. He will give pop quizzes if he suspects that no one has read the readings. Also, he doesn't play about attendance and expects students to be on time. Tough at grading papers.

Dr. Ashe is undoubtedly brilliant. You MUST participate -- come very well prepared to class, ask thoughtful questions, provide thoughtful feedback. Don't do anything late. Always ask for advice. Don't be intimidated or embarrassed or afraid to be wrong. Trust me, you'll be wrong.
Participate in class. Do the reading. Don't complain. Ask for advice on papers.

Dr. Ashe was an amazing professor! He really values your opinion and participation is a huge part of your grade. There is a large amount of reading and you read a whole book in a week. He forces you to think outside of the box and has superior analytical skills. He is also a very tough grader, so go to the writing center! Overall he was great!

Dr. Ashe made what would typically be a boring literature class immensely interesting. Participation is critical and papers are long and extremely tough. He really challenges your ability to analyze text.

The Black Vernacular was one of the most fascinating classes I have ever taken. Class is always captivating and you are expected to participate as class is 100% discussion based. 2 papers and the final is a take home paper. He's a tough grader, be prepared for that.

hes awesome. very deep thinker and super smart. if u read closely & go to class ready to participate, class is enjoyable. 3 papers that were all kind of variations on same topic to some extent. fair, consistent grader. very enthusiastic about what he teaches, which makes u want to try harder. read a book a week, then discuss for a week. got A-.

Class is extremely difficult and challenging. His research paper is the hardest paper I have ever written in college. Very hard grader. You learn a lot, though. Just be prepared to put a LOT of effort into this class, though.

Dictatorial command of the class. Is not concerned with individual interpretation unless it coincides with his narrow-minded & typically arbitrary analysis of the text. Syllabus includes great works but he spends so little time on eachtext and you won't even write on books heteaches in class. He ruined my desire to pursue English/read great novels.

Took him 3x, one for 200, twice for 3, loved every second of all of them. Total badass. Most engaging professor EVER, class is all discussion; don't come prepared to actively contribute and youre f-ed. Only 2 papers and a final (which is usually 2 4-pagers). Unlike any other class you'll take at Richmond. English majors, he's a must.

I was terrified that I would fail after the first day of the class. However, as time went on, I discovered that Ashe wanted us to actually LEARN how to think in new ways, not just pass his class. If you're looking for an experience different from the typical course at Richmond, take him. Oh, and I got an A in the class...
Class is 100% discussion. Midterm and Final are take home. 2 other papers. Never get out of class early. Expects your best.

By far the most engaging teacher at richmond.  His classes are entirely discussion, so you better be ready to contribute.  Funny, very very smart but he doesn't use his knowledge to be imperious and show off, he uses it to help you better understand the material.
Great prof - recommend, the class was fun, he is energetic and always willing to meet with students about papers, etc.
Good teacher who knows what he is talking about, very willing to help out.  He most wants you to participate and express your thoughts to everyone and get the class involved!

Professor Ashe is cool, down to earth, and funny.  He knows how to get an entire class out of their "bubble" by getting everyone to participate. His vibrant personality makes class interesting.  Reading, participation, and a few papers is all that is required, but Prof. A demands your best.
